campaign: MOSS in overgo does what the MOSS Ultra workflow does in ComfyUI, each section held to ComfyUI's recording

items.title: A MOSS run reports the prompt and negative prompt it drew from, and the page shows them and offers them back as the manual prompt

steps.title: The page shows a MOSS run's prompt and negative prompt used and offers each back as the manual prompt
steps.rationale: The page half of moss-prompts-used: a completed run shows "Prompt used" and "Negative prompt used" as the workflow's PreviewAny nodes do, and a control sets the manual prompt and negative from them, so an enhanced or built prompt can be edited and drawn again in mode 1.

items.title: MOSS's page offers one prompt mode, manual, enhanced or builder, showing only that mode's fields, declared by the control list so the page stays generated

steps.title: The MOSS control list declares one prompt mode choice of manual, enhanced and builder, and the fields each shows
steps.rationale:
The owner's review of 2026-11-22, point 3, checked against the code: valid. The workflow chooses one prompt mode (manual, enhanced by its chat, or built from the Ideogram builder's layout). A rotary model's page offers three controls for it side by side (mediacapability imageControls, rotaryControls): prompt_mode, whose choices text and layout select a validation and rewrite nothing (latentimage PromptMode), enhance, a boolean, and layout, an object; a Control declares no field that shows another only for one choice, so the page cannot show one mode's fields alone.

The change: the control list offers one mode choice and declares, for each choice, the fields it shows (the prompt and negative for manual and enhanced, the layout for the builder), and a request is taken as the chosen mode sets it.

Check: TestMOSSOffersOnePromptModeShowingItsFields, card-free.

steps.title: Choosing a MOSS prompt mode shows only its fields, as the control list declares them
steps.rationale: The page half of moss-prompt-mode: the page reads which fields each mode shows from the control list (it generates its controls, and names no MOSS field itself), and each mode's request reaches the session as that mode's.

items.title: A sharpened MOSS run returns its drawn picture and its sharpened picture, compared on the page as the workflow compares them

steps.title: A sharpened MOSS picture returns the picture it drew beside the sharpened one, the drawn one bit for bit the same request's unsharpened picture
steps.rationale:
The owner's review of 2026-11-22, point 4, checked against the code and the workflow: valid. Each of the workflow's six sections saves its decoded picture and its ImageSharpen's picture (twelve SaveImage nodes: text to image 449 and 482, its Turbo 86 and 147, image to image 512 and 604, its Turbo 214 and 344, depth control 445 and 610, its Turbo 50 and 364), and its Image Comparer shows them against each other (709, 324, 605, 345) or, in the depth sections, each against the section's source (611 and 669, 365 and 423). overgo sharpens the decoded pixels in place as it finishes the picture (generator_rotary_windows.go, media.Sharpen) and returns the sharpened picture alone. The page's A/B compare (generation.js abCompare) cites nodes 611 and 669 as comparing a section's picture against the one it started from, which only the depth sections do.

The change: a run with sharpening returns both pictures, the drawn one first, each recorded as an output of the run.

Check: TestASharpenedPictureReturnsThePictureItDrew on the compact MOSS fixture, a short card test.

steps.title: The page compares a sharpened run's drawn and sharpened pictures with its A/B slider, as each section's comparer does
steps.rationale: The page half of moss-sharpened-pair: a run returning both pictures opens the existing A/B compare with the drawn picture as A and the sharpened as B, and abCompare's comment states the workflow's comparers as they are.

items.title: Every node by which the MOSS Ultra workflow saves, previews, compares or shows something has its counterpart in a run's result or on the page, and one without is refused without the card

steps.title: Every node by which the MOSS Ultra workflow saves, previews, compares or shows something has its counterpart in a run's result or on the page, and one without is refused without the card
steps.rationale:
How the review's points 2 and 4 went unseen: the sections were held to ComfyUI's pictures, and what the workflow shows beside them was read from a few of its nodes (abCompare cites the depth section's comparers for every section), so its twelve PreviewAny prompt displays and its six saves of the unsharpened picture had no counterpart and no check said so. The workflow's sections hold 12 SaveImage, 2 PreviewImage, 12 PreviewAny and 10 Image Comparer (rgthree) nodes.

The change: a table names, for each such node of each section's request (fixtures/comfy/moss-ultra/requests), the result field or page element that does what it does, or why it has none (an intermediate preview); the check reads the requests and refuses a node of those classes the table does not name, and a named counterpart the page or result does not hold. Filed last of the review's rows: it holds what they add.

items.title: SenseNova's request-resources test is measured again on a card to itself and carries modeltest, so the gate's cuda lane runs no real-model test

steps.title: SenseNova's request-resources test is measured again on a card to itself and carries modeltest, so the gate's cuda lane runs no real-model test
steps.rationale:
The evidence: cuda-synthetic/tag moved every untagged CUDA test that reads the data root behind modeltest but one. TestSenseNovaVariableRequestResources runs SenseNova's 8B production generation in an isolated measurement process, and docs/image_video_capacity.json names its retained measurement by the bytes of its file (evidence:sha256:888854b5...), which the store holds; tagged, its bytes changed and TestImageVideoCapacityAcceptance found no evidence under the new identity. A measurement is taken again only on a card to itself, and the readings campaign holds the card until its Wan arms are drawn, so the file stays in the gate, named by the check as measuredInPlace, and this row follows the campaign.

The change: the test carries //go:build modeltest, it is measured again on a quiet card into the store, the capacity record and its protocol digest (imageVideoCapacitySHA256) name the new identity, and measuredInPlace goes, so internal/sensenovarecipe leaves the cuda lane.

Check: a whole-tree test with measuredInPlace gone, named afresh so it fails before the change: TestTheGateRunsNoRealModelTest.

Refiled 2026-11-16 from cuda-resources/do, whose step carried no card need, so dispatch gave it while the readings campaign held the card: this step carries -needs-card and waits for a card to itself.

decisions.question: skill.md's 227 rule lines each cite a check. Read at 3ba4de8c7: the first check of 181 has a doc comment and of 45 has none, and the comments state what their test holds, not the rule that cites it ("purpose = recursive self-improvement ..." cites TestCycleFilesDeclinesAndAcceptsNothing, whose comment is the cycle's comparisons; "scorecard columns = ..." cites TestScorecardRowsEveryServableModel, whose comment is rows and dashes). Writing skill.md from the comments as they stand changes what it says. Which form does skill.md take?
options: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
skill.md holds its terms and judgement lines alone; the rule lines go, each check saying its rule when it refuses
skill.md is written from the tests' doc comments as they stand, its wording changing to theirs
decisions.recommendation: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
